programmes.funder: Smart Capital / Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations de Tunisie, with the World Bank and European partners
programmes.amount_note: A fund of funds that capitalises Tunisian venture funds, which in turn invest in labelled and other Tunisian startups. Startups do not apply to ANAVA directly.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; approach the ANAVA-backed fund managers.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach the manager with your round.

eligibility.other_note: Tunisian startups; holding the Startup Act label improves access but is not always mandatory.

programmes.funder: Ministère des Technologies de la Communication / Smart Capital, Tunisia
programmes.amount_note: Labelled startups receive a package rather than a single grant: a founder's allowance (bourse de startup) paid monthly for up to one year to up to three founders, an eight-year corporate tax exemption, state coverage of social contributions, a special foreign currency account, and the right for public-sector or company employees to take a one-year startup leave with salary continuity.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are submitted continuously on the Startup Tunisia portal and reviewed by a labelling committee (Comité de Labellisation) that meets in periodic sessions.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the company in Tunisia (or apply as a project about to be registered).
Create an account on startup.gov.tn and submit the label application.
Review by the Comité de Labellisation at its next session.
Label granted for eight years; then claim the individual benefits from the relevant administrations.

eligibility.other_note: Company must be under 8 years old, have no more than 100 employees, total assets and turnover below defined ceilings, be majority owned by natural persons or qualifying investors, and have an innovative and scalable business model.

programmes.source_snippet: Discover the many advantages offered by the Startup Act
